clue.text: Soldier survives dramatic event in theatre

parts.note: a private is the lowest rank of soldier
to survive is to go on living, so survives gives lives

explanation.surface: A soldier comes through some dramatic incident while serving in a theatre of war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' suggests a theatre of war; it is the stage, where PRIVATE LIVES is Noel Coward's comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel Coward's comedy is a play, a dramatic piece staged at a playhouse.

clue.text: Log table

definitions.meaning: to log something is to record it, write it down
to table a motion is to submit it formally for debate

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean to enter in writing: record an item, or submit a motion for debate.

clue.text: Girl stifling pain put up epic struggle

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the whole construction is read from the bottom upwards
stifling means smothering, so the girl's name wraps round the pain word

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name
to ail is to cause pain

explanation.surface: A girl suppresses her pain and puts up a heroic fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stifling' gives DAILI and 'put up' turns it round; 'struggle' belongs with 'epic' in the definition, not the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's poem is an epic about the long war at Troy, a struggle in verse.

clue.text: Girl one abandoned in foreign port

indicators.note: abandoned means left behind, so the numeral is dropped from the port's name

parts.note: Alexandria is a great Egyptian port
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A girl, on her own, has been left behind in a port overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' drops I from ALEXANDRIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandra is a woman's given name, so it fits a girl.

clue.text: Insignificant penniless artist

indicators.note: penniless means without a penny, and P is the abbreviation for penny, so that letter goes

parts.note: petty means trivial or unimportant

explanation.surface: A minor painter without any money to his name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penniless' removes P (penny) from PETTY. William Etty was a 19th-century English painter.
explanation.definitionFit: William Etty was an English painter known for nudes, so he is an artist.

clue.text: Doctor getting into hot water

indicators.note: getting into means entering, so the falsify word goes inside the angry word

parts.note: hot under the collar means angry, irate
to doctor results is to rig or falsify them

explanation.surface: A physician ends up in trouble, in hot water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' and 'hot water' suggest a medic in trouble; 'Doctor' is the verb rig, put inside IRATE by 'getting into'.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrigate land is to supply it with water through channels.

clue.text: Obvious I'd scratched from contest

indicators.note: a runner scratched from a race is withdrawn, so these letters are taken out

parts.note: evident means plain or obvious
taken as written, the letters I and D

explanation.surface: Plainly, I've been withdrawn from the competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scratched from' removes ID from EVIDENT; 'scratched' is racing slang for withdrawn.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is a single competition, such as a race in an athletics meeting.

clue.text: Digs for foreign coins

definitions.meaning: digs is informal British for lodgings, a place to stay
a US quarter is a 25-cent coin, foreign from a British point of view

explanation.definitionFit: Lodgings are rooms to live in, and the US twenty-five-cent pieces are coins abroad.

clue.text: Family tree, say

indicators.note: say signals that the tree's name is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: the peepul is the sacred fig tree of India

explanation.surface: A family tree, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Family tree' looks like one phrase; 'Family' is the definition and the tree is the peepul, an Indian fig.
explanation.definitionFit: One's people are one's relatives or kin, as in taking someone home to meet the folks.

clue.text: Term for an American scholar

parts.note: reads like a request for a US word meaning scholar, but describes one of the three periods into which some US colleges divide the academic year

explanation.definitionFit: Some American colleges divide their year into three study periods, each a term for students there.

clue.text: Start off kid's puzzle

indicators.note: start off means the first letter is removed from the fooling word

parts.note: to kid someone is to delude or fool them

explanation.surface: Kick off a children's brainteaser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start off kid's puzzle' reads as beginning a child's game; 'Start off' drops D from DELUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To elude someone is to baffle or escape their understanding, as a riddle can.

clue.text: Unfashionable lad getting hot and bothered

indicators.note: hot and bothered means flustered, so the letters before it are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned boy getting worked up and flustered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot and bothered' looks like one phrase; 'hot' is fodder and 'and bothered' signals the anagram of LAD and HOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something old hat is outdated, out of fashion, no longer stylish.

clue.text: Information calculated to make one go red

definitions.text: Information calculated to make one go red

parts.words: Information calculated to make one go red
parts.note: sounds like embarrassing news that makes someone blush, but means material meant to convert someone to communism

explanation.definitionFit: Agitprop is political propaganda, originally Soviet, spread to win people over to communism.

clue.text: Number, figure and cipher

parts.note: a figure is a body, a person's shape

explanation.surface: A list of a number, a figure and a code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cipher' looks like a code but here means a person of no importance.
explanation.definitionFit: A cipher is a person of no importance, an insignificant figure.

clue.text: Heather, placed under arrest, is lively

indicators.note: in a down clue, placed under means the plant goes below the arrest word

parts.note: a bust is slang for a police arrest
ling is a common heather

explanation.surface: A woman called Heather is put under arrest, and is full of energy about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name; it is the plant, LING.
explanation.definitionFit: A bustling place or person is busy and full of energetic activity.

clue.text: Impressed by aeroplane's last uncontrollable flight

indicators.note: by means beside, so the letter is put next to the stamped word

parts.note: to impress a mark is to stamp it

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the aircraft word

explanation.surface: Someone is impressed by a plane's final runaway flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests an aeroplane, but it is fleeing.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden panicked rush, as of a herd fleeing in terror.

clue.text: Computer graduate put in case

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate
taken as written
a case or casing is a frame round something

explanation.surface: A computer graduate gets put in a case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Computer graduate' looks like a single phrase; 'Computer' is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A mainframe is a large central computer serving many users.

clue.text: Drawing most of map without a mountain pass

indicators.note: most of means the word is used without its final letter

parts.note: a chart is a map, especially at sea

indicators.note: without means outside, so the pass goes round the letter

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: A sketch made from most of a map that leaves out a mountain pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking; 'most of' cuts the last letter of the map word.
explanation.definitionFit: A charcoal is a sketch made with burnt-wood sticks.

clue.text: Provide full coverage with articles on all points

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so the articles follow the compass points

parts.note: E, N, S and W are the four compass points
a and the are the indefinite and definite articles

explanation.surface: A newspaper promises full coverage, with stories on every point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' suggests newspaper stories; they are the grammatical articles A and THE, after the compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: To enswathe is to wrap or swaddle completely, covering something entirely.

clue.text: Former African National Park

parts.note: ex means former
a Moor is a North African

explanation.surface: A one-time African national park.
explanation.walkthrough: EXMOOR is a national park in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Exmoor is a moorland area in Somerset and Devon designated a national park in England.

clue.text: Take time to publish paper

parts.note: to issue a book is to publish it

explanation.surface: Take your time before publishing a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paper' suggests a newspaper; it is fine paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue is thin soft paper, used for wrapping or as handkerchiefs.

clue.text: Lost chapter inserted into text in novel

indicators.note: inserted into means the abbreviation goes inside the jumbled letters
novel means new, so the letters before it are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A missing chapter has been put back into the text of a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' makes EXTINT, and 'inserted into' places the chapter letter inside it; 'Lost' means died out, not mislaid.
explanation.definitionFit: An extinct species has died out, gone for good.

clue.text: Meal part cooked with lots of sauce

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or doctored, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Part of a meal is cooked with plenty of gravy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sauce' looks like gravy; it is cheek or impudence.
explanation.definitionFit: Malapert is an archaic word for impudent or cheeky, full of sauce.

clue.text: Annoy gym mistress in the garden

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym
Eve was the woman in the Garden of Eden

explanation.surface: Irritate the gym teacher out in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gym mistress' looks like one phrase, a PE teacher; 'mistress in the garden' is Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: To peeve is to irritate or vex someone.

clue.text: Compensate for being high-class

parts.note: high meat has gone off
a set is a class or group, as in school

explanation.surface: Making up for one's upper-class status.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high-class' looks like one word; split it, with high meaning spoiled, as meat goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To offset a loss is to counterbalance or make up for it.

clue.text: County is upset about losing opening game

indicators.note: about means around, so the turned word surrounds a letter
in a down clue, upset means the word is turned upside down
opening points to the first letter of losing

parts.note: Go is a Japanese board game

explanation.surface: A county is upset about losing its opening match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' makes SI and 'about' puts the opening of 'losing' inside it. SLIGO is an Irish county.
explanation.definitionFit: Sligo is a county in north-west Ireland.

clue.text: Come together in reportedly drunken confusion

indicators.note: reportedly drunken means the word is said as a drunk would slur it

parts.note: a mess is a state of confusion

explanation.surface: Gather together amid tipsy chaos, people say.
explanation.walkthrough: A drunk slurs the S of MESS into SH.
explanation.definitionFit: Gears mesh when their teeth engage, fitting together.

clue.text: Wildcat strike without a leader

indicators.note: without a leader means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: to pounce is to strike suddenly

explanation.surface: A wildcat strike is called with no union leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wildcat strike' looks like an unofficial walkout; 'Wildcat' is the definition, the snow leopard.
explanation.definitionFit: The ounce is the snow leopard, a big wild cat of Central Asia.

clue.text: Handling a relationship in public

indicators.note: in means the relationship word goes inside the public word

parts.note: something open is public, not secret
a ratio is a numerical relationship between quantities

explanation.surface: Conducting an affair openly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relationship' suggests romance; it is a mathematical ratio.
explanation.definitionFit: An operation is the working or handling of a machine or system.

clue.text: Smashing hotel's rather a good place to get fit

definitions.text: a good place to get fit

indicators.note: smashing means breaking apart, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written with its S
taken as written

explanation.surface: A smashing hotel is rather a good place to get in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashing' reads as praise of the hotel; it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa town or retreat is somewhere people go to improve their fitness.
